claims.text: setState calls the given function synchronously, then marks the State's element dirty so build runs again before Flutter next draws the screen (next frame).
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: State.setState ('The provided callback is immediately called synchronously… causes the framework to schedule a build')

claims.text: Changing a State field without setState does not cause a rebuild; the change shows only at the next build triggered by something else.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: State.setState ('If you just change the state directly without calling setState, the framework might not schedule a build')

claims.text: setState rebuilds the calling State and updates the widgets below it; ancestors are not rebuilt. At stage-1, DonHangApp.build returns the MaterialApp whose home is ProductListScreen, so both sit above it.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: State.setState, State.build; refs/flutter-website ui/interactivity; examples/don-hang @ stage-1 DonHang.App/lib/main.dart

claims.text: _reload is `setState(() { _products = widget.apiClient.fetchProducts(); })` (block body; the `=>` belongs to _reload), _products is a Future, and the refresh FloatingActionButton's onPressed is _reload.

FutureBuilder shows a loading indicator (in this screen's builder) while its future is unfinished and the list once done; given a new future it goes back to waiting, and its own State calls setState when the future completes.

LoginScreen._submit begins with one setState setting _loading = true and _error = null; build reads _loading to disable the button and show a loading indicator instead of its label, and _error to decide whether the error Text is shown.
A field changed without setState shows up at a later build of this screen caused by something else; FutureBuilder then gets the new future, shows the loading indicator, then the new list.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: MediaQuery-dependent widgets rebuild on size change (MaterialApp/Scaffold depend on MediaQuery)

claims.text: Rebuilding only the changed subtree keeps small changes cheap.

A setState callback must not return a Future (unclear when the state was set); in debug mode Flutter asserts "setState() callback argument returned a Future". An arrow callback assigning a Future returns it; a block body returns nothing.
claims.source_hint: Flutter State.setState docs ('It must not return a future… since then it would be unclear when the state was actually being set') and assert

claims.text: setState in _submit runs before the request starts; the rebuild shows in the next frame while the request is in progress.
claims.source_hint: State.setState marks dirty; build on next frame
